newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Missing Briton fails to show in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Missing Briton fails to show in Cambodia.

text.p: The fate of Briton Christopher Howes and his Cambodian interpreter remained unclear on Friday night after the two men failed to arrive in Phnom Penh as expected after reportedly escaping from hardline Khmer Rouge guerrillas.

General Prom Sanein, deputy commander of the military region centred around the northwest province of Siem Reap, said his men were waiting for Howes, a mine clearance expert, his interpreter Houn Hourth and Khmer Rouge defectors in a northern Cambodian village.

"Some of my force are in Anlong Kranh to greet them but until now there is no news from them," he told Reuters from Siem Reap hours after another general had said he expected Howes to arrive in the capital on Friday after eight months of captivity.

Howes and his interpreter were abducted by armed men in the northwest province of Siem Reap on March 26 as they were working with colleagues on a humanitarian mine-clearing mission near the famed Angkor temples for the Mines Advisory Group (MAG) of Britain.
Nhiek Bun Chhay, deputy chief of general staff, told Reuters that Howes and Houn Hourth would arrive at the Phnom Penh military airport on Friday afternoon, but the two men never came.
Nhiek Bun Chhay said the two men escaped from the Khmer Rouge base at Anlong Veng near the Thai border on November 5 with the help of their guards and guerrilla defectors.
While thin, they were in good health, he said.
The two men had reached Anlong Kranh village in central Kompong Thom province in the company of 151 Khmer Rouge guards and defectors, Nhiek Bun Chhay said.
But Prom Sanein said on Friday that he was still waiting for the hostages and the Khmer Rouge defectors in the village, located in jungle some 185 km (115 miles) north of Phnom Penh.
Meanwhile, a top official said the government was prepared to reward the men who released the two hostages.

"We are ready to reward them after their arrival because they not only defected but also accomplished the major achievement of bringing the foreign mine clearer," co-Defence Minister Tea Banh told Reuters.
Tea Banh said Howes' Khmer Rouge companions -- reportedly 151 fighters, including 11 guards and a divisional commander -- would also be inducted into the Cambodian armed forces.

MAG and the British Embassy have treated reports of the escape with caution and MAG's programme director, Archie McCarron, told Reuters on Friday evening that reports of the men's release remained unconfirmed.
